entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Johann Heß (1500-1547) was a German Lutheran theologian and Protestant Reformer of Breslau. Born in the Holy Roman Empire, Heß studied at the University of Leipzig and later became a prominent figure in the Lutheran movement.

 Heß's most significant contribution to the Protestant Reformation was his translation of the Bible into German, which made scripture more accessible to ordinary people. His work also emphasized the importance of personal faith and spiritual discipline, influencing many subsequent Lutheran theologians.

 As a key figure associated with the Breslau movement, Heß played a crucial role in shaping the theological landscape of 16th-century Germany. His legacy continues to be felt today, particularly in the realm of Lutheran theology and biblical studies.

 In his own words, 'The Word of God is not just a book, but a living, breathing presence that guides us on our spiritual journey.' - Johann Heß

entities.name: Johann Heß
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Johann Heß was a German Lutheran theologian and Protestant Reformer of Breslau, born on October 2, 1490, in Nuremberg, and died on January 15, 1547. He played a significant role in the Protestant Reformation, contributing to the development of the Lutheran Church. His influence extended to the spread of Protestantism in Central Europe, particularly in Silesia and Brandenburg.

Heß was influenced by the ideas of Martin Luther and participated in the Council of Trent, where he advocated for Lutheran reforms. His theological works, such as 'De Sacramentis,' shaped the understanding of sacraments in the Lutheran Church.

Heß's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Lutheran Reformation on Protestant denominations in Europe and beyond. His work on sacraments has also been recognized as a key aspect of Lutheran theology.

In a surprising twist, Heß's theological contributions were not widely recognized during his lifetime, and it was not until the 19th century that his work gained significant attention.
